'''Decipher mailing lists''' were the e-mail discussion lists run by [[Decipher]] for players of the ''[[Star Wars CCG|Star Wars Customizable Card Game]]'' and its other games. From 1996 the company ran Majordomo lists at games.decipher.com, including '''swccg-discussion''' for rules and strategy talk and '''swccg-marketplace''' for trading. Decipher sponsored the lists officially but did not moderate them, and the Star Wars CCG "Netrep" answered rules questions on swccg-discussion.<ref name="egfull">[http://www.egroups.com/group/swccg-discussion/fullinfo.html swccg-discussion group info], eGroups (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991010040911/http://www.egroups.com:80/group/swccg-discussion/fullinfo.html Internet Archive]</ref> Around 2002 the lists moved to a GNU Mailman server at lists.decipher.com.<ref name="mm">[http://lists.decipher.com/mailman/listinfo/swccg-discussion Swccg-discussion Info Page], Decipher (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020612121031/http://lists.decipher.com:80/mailman/listinfo/swccg-discussion Internet Archive]</ref>

== History ==
In 1997 Decipher's ''Star Wars CCG'' "Dialog" page listed the "Listserv", the emailback document service and the faxback service as sources of information. It placed them alongside the bulletin boards and the Star Wars Palace chat. A web form sent subscribe and unsubscribe commands to majordomo@decipher.com. Every list also had a digest version.<ref name="dialog">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/dialog/listserv/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game : Dialog], Decipher (1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970607094559/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/dialog/listserv/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> On the matching Star Trek page, Decipher explained that a digest arrived "in bundles of 50 messages each".<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/startrek/dialog/listserv/index.html Star Trek Customizable Card Game : Dialog], Decipher (1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970607094352/http://www.decipher.com:80/startrek/dialog/listserv/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> In 1999 the Young Jedi lists were added, and the subscription form moved to the Message Boards section.<ref name="mb99">[http://www.decipher.com/messageboards/mailinglists/index.html Message Boards : Mailing Lists], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990910234435/http://www1.decipher.com:80/messageboards/mailinglists/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

swccg-discussion was very busy. Between January 1997 and December 1998 it carried about 67,000 messages, with more than 4,000 a month at its peak in mid-1998.<ref name="yg">[http://groups.yahoo.com/group/swccg-discussion swccg-discussion], Yahoo! Groups (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010506001004/http://groups.yahoo.com:80/group/swccg-discussion Internet Archive]</ref> Frequent posters included Justin Pakes and Mark Tuttle.

Decipher's Mailman server, lists.decipher.com, hosted discussion and marketplace lists for each game: Star Wars, Star Trek, Young Jedi, Jedi Knights and The Lord of the Rings TCG. Only list members could read the archives.<ref name="mm" /> From 2002 Decipher also ran short-term "insider" or "news blast" lists for new expansions and events. In September 2004 it set up the dAgent and dAgent-intl lists for its volunteer program, run by Kyle Heuer and Kim Logie.<ref name="dagent">[http://lists.decipher.com/mailman/listinfo/dagent Dagent Info Page], Decipher (2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041205104600/http://lists.decipher.com:80/mailman/listinfo/dagent Internet Archive]</ref>

== Archives ==
Decipher's own archives of the game lists were private and do not survive. The most important surviving record is an eGroups (later Yahoo! Groups) mirror of swccg-discussion, which was subscribed to the Decipher list as a "remote list". It held messages 1 to 67,554, from 7 January 1997 to 5 December 1998.<ref name="egidx">[http://www.egroups.com/group/swccg-discussion/ swccg-discussion messages], eGroups (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991010033046/http://www.egroups.com:80/group/swccg-discussion/ Internet Archive]</ref> The Internet Archive saved several hundred individual message pages from the mirror. The first is a rules post by Justin Pakes titled "R units". The 428 recovered messages are indexed on [[Decipher swccg-discussion list archive]].<ref>[http://www.egroups.com/group/swccg-discussion/1.html swccg-discussion message #1], eGroups (1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991222214202/http://www.egroups.com:80/group/swccg-discussion/1.html? Internet Archive]</ref>

The public Pipermail archive of the dAgent list survives in full: 2,092 messages from September 2004 to January 2005, mostly about ''WARS'' and ''The Lord of the Rings'' TCG.<ref>[http://lists.decipher.com/pipermail/dagent/ The Dagent Archives], Decipher (2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041205172920/http://lists.decipher.com:80/pipermail/dagent/ Internet Archive]</ref>
